brief:
## Summary

Migrate billing records to a multi-tenant schema so a single billing event stream can serve all tenants instead of one database per tenant.

## Decisions so far

- Rollout ships behind a per-tenant feature flag (not a single global cutover).
- Marcus Webb owns the backfill script for existing single-tenant rows.

## Still open

- Whether the billing event schema needs a version bump to support dual-writes during migration.

## Conflicts to resolve

The ticket description has not been updated to reflect the per-tenant rollout decision or the likely schema version bump. See the Overview tab for details.
plan:
## Rollout plan

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["Add tenant_id column (nullable)"] --> B["Backfill existing rows"]
  B --> C["Bump billing event schema to v3"]
  C --> D["Dual-write new billing events"]
  D --> E["Verify parity report per tenant"]
  E --> F["Enable per-tenant feature flag"]
  F --> G["Remove legacy single-tenant path"]
```

### Steps

1. Add a nullable `tenant_id` column to the billing tables.
2. Run the backfill script (owner: Marcus Webb) against existing single-tenant rows.
3. Bump the billing event schema to v3 to carry `tenant_id`.
4. Start dual-writing new billing events to both the legacy and multi-tenant paths.
5. Run a parity report per tenant before enabling the flag for that tenant.
6. Enable the per-tenant feature flag once parity is confirmed.
7. Remove the legacy single-tenant code path after all tenants are migrated.

### Risks

- Dual-write window increases write latency; needs a load test before enabling broadly.
- Backfill script must be idempotent in case it needs to be re-run after a schema bump.
